actualSelectedScientificInspection: Six carbon centers each have exactly one C-H bond and two ring sigma connections.

Energy comparison places the delocalized model below the hypothetical localized model; no numerical experimental claim or activation pathway.

actualSelectedScientificInspection: Incoming benzene has three alternating pi bonds.

The product restores three alternating double bonds and retains E but no H at the substitution carbon.
Minus-H-plus label denotes proton loss, not hydride departure. Straight arrows are reaction arrows, not curved electron-pair arrows.

concreteRejectedAttempt.finding: Generic Ar-H coupling ended in unsubstituted diphenyl azo structure without an explicit activated partner; could suggest unactivated benzene is a suitable azo coupling partner.

actualSelectedScientificInspection: Left reactants explicitly identify benzenediazonium and phenol.
Azo product has two neutral nitrogens with one N=N double bond and one aryl single bond each.
OH is para to azo attachment on the phenol-derived ring; formal coupling plus H+ balances composition/net charge.
Right leuco central C has exactly four bonds to Ph,Ar,Ar,H; final C+ has exactly three bonds to Ph,Ar,Ar and no H.
Two routes occupy distinct columns; there is no arrow transforming an azo dye into a triarylmethane dye.
records.actualResponsiveFinding: At360 the azo bridge/paraOH and four-bond to three-bond carbon motif remain countable; compact aryl abbreviations are support labels. At680 all formula, charge and bond relationships can be inspected.
limitations: Ar denotes suitable donor-substituted aryl residues,Ph denotes phenyl; icons are residue placeholders,not complete unsubstituted ring structures.
Right route is intentionally abbreviated: water,oxidant,proton/electron balance and counterions are omitted,so the arrows are not a full stoichiometric equation.
Green highlight is a didactic color accent,not a claim of photon emission.
